assertions.interpretation: Wang Rong states that since the beginning of the Han dynasty (漢元) there has been no one like Ruan Wenyè, providing a historical backdrop against which Ruan's qualities are measured.
The annotation notes that Ruan Wu (阮武) served as Prefect of Heqing at the end of the Wei dynasty (魏末), placing his official career in the late Wei period.
The annotation describes that when Guo Tai (郭泰) was still young (at the age of 總角, i.e., childhood), he was not yet famous, and Ruan Wu recognized his worth at that time.
The annotation records that Ruan Wu ultimately died at home (終於家), a later outcome of his life.
The annotation fragment references Guo Tai (泰) in relation to the period since the beginning of the Han dynasty (漢元以來), echoing the main text's historical framing.
